prompt: make a game within the confines and abilities of my engine

promptTranslations.en: make a game within the confines and abilities of my engine

summary: gsimone prompted Opus 5.5 to create a game within the limits and capabilities of their custom engine, resulting in a deep-sea horror game with an ambient drone soundtrack.

post.originalText: I asked opus 5.5 to make a game within the confines and abilities of my engine, no other prompt. It made this deep-sea horror game, with a subtle drone soundtrack. And it's terrifying (if a bit unbalanced/unfair). Sound on. https://t.co/PJmQ7v0ZIN

sourceMaterials.text: @Jaenam97 yeah this was my cleanse from that, I'm so tired of that kind of slop. 3D lends itself very well to looking like shit, as you surely know. It takes a LOT of effort to make 3D shit that doesn't look ridiculous. I think we need to embrace the tools more widely
sourceMaterials.author: ggsimm

sourceMaterials.text: @Jaenam97 Just random stuff I like that I know agents work well with - I used all the pieces individually before. The choice of ascii is just to have a coherent look throughout the games, I’m playing with size of color palette and resolution and it’s quite flexible
sourceMaterials.author: ggsimm

sourceMaterials.text: It built almost no new capabilities btw, just reused the lib I built while making all the other ones - particles, illumination, projectiles, collisions etc
sourceMaterials.author: ggsimm

sourceMaterials.text: interestingly, the heels/sea monsters will go towards the ping, they are blind - so you can trick them by pinging and taking a longer route around them
sourceMaterials.author: ggsimm

sourceMaterials.text: the fact it used my tiny sfx engine to make some kind of bgm is crazy to me, so cool
